title: Spectradyne nCS1: Sample Measurement and Device Maintenance Protocol
author: Bryce Killingsworth
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmx8k7rw

Wait about three minutes for routine to finish.
Enter mold ID and box ID information into the nCS1 software.

The bar at the top of the software should be green with the word "Ready" displayed. If not, shut off the nCS1, restart the PC and then repeat the power up process, ensuring the software is only opened after the nCS1 is powered on and properly connected via its USB cable.

steps.title: Prepare Running Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh running buffer if the current buffer is more than two weeks old.

substeps.instruction: Discard old running buffer from nCS1 buffer bottles.
Rinse buffer bottles with a small amount of purified/filtered water.
If needed, prepare 500 mL of 1% Tween-20 by pipetting 5 mL of pure Tween-20 into a new sterile 500 mL bottle of DPBS.
Invert the bottle occasionally for at least 15 minutes until Tween-20 is entirely dissolved.
Filter half of the 1% (v/v) Tween-20 solution using a 0.2 µm PES bottle-top filter.
Equally divide the filtered 1% (v/v) Tween-20 solution into the two nCS1 buffer bottles.
Store running buffer at 4 °C and mark the preparation date.

steps.title: Initialize Instrument
steps.instruction: Power on the system and set up the fluidics.

substeps.instruction: Turn on and log in to the attached PC.
Retrieve nCS1 buffer bottles and water bottles from the 4 °C fridge.
Attach buffer bottles to the indicated fluid lines on the side of the instrument, ensuring caps are screwed on tightly to prevent pressure leaks.
Turn on the nCS1 using the power switch on the back of the instrument.

steps.title: Perform Initial Cleaning
steps.instruction: Clean the device using a cleaning cartridge, recommended at every instrument startup.

substeps.instruction: Position a cleaning cartridge in the stage slot until the blue indicator light and blue ring light illuminate.
Press the outside button to raise the stage.
Click 'run cleaning cartridge' in the software.
Press the metal button to lower the stage and return the cartridge to storage.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample solution and spike-in beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1.0% (v/v) Tween-20 in Thermo Fisher Gibco Sterile DPBS (PBST) or a 0.1% (v/v) BSA in Thermo Fisher Gibco Sterile DPBS, allowing solids to dissolve.
Filter the solution using a Whatman Anotop 10, 0.02 µm syringe-driven filter into clean plastic tubes.

Calculate volumes for filtered 1% (v/v) Tween/PBS, spike-in beads, and sample particles. Suggested final concentrations: spike-in beads 5E9 particles/mL, sample particles ~1E10 particles/mL, with a total volume of at least 50 µL.
Select spike-in beads based on cartridge: 203 nm NIST PS for C-300 cartridges or 269 nm NIST PS for C-400 cartridges.
Vortex spike-in beads (e.g., 10 short pulses at max power) and pipette into 1% (v/v) Tween/PBS buffer; vortex thoroughly to avoid aggregates.
Vortex sample particles and pipette into the buffer/bead mixture; vortex well.

steps.title: Load Sample Cartridge
steps.instruction: Load the prepared sample into a new cartridge without introducing air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a new sample cartridge and set a P10 pipette to 4 µL.
Vortex the sample particle mixture immediately before drawing up 4 µL, ensuring no air bubbles are in the tip.
Hold the cartridge in place and insert the pipette tip into the fluid loading aperture until it gently contacts the bottom of the loading chamber.
Slowly pull the tip upward while loading ~3.5 µL of sample into the bottom of the cartridge, leaving a small volume in the tip to avoid pipetting an air bubble.
Tap the cartridge against the table to dislodge bubbles and inspect the meniscus at eye level.
If bubbles persist, tap again or use the P10 pipette to aspirate and retry.
Insert the cartridge onto the stage and verify the blue indicator dot and blue ring light are illuminated.

steps.title: Configure Software and Run
steps.instruction: Set up the data files and begin the automated measurement process.

substeps.instruction: Record sample information in the nCS1 Cartridge Log (SharePoint) or a personal log including lot numbers.
Enter a descriptive prefix and optional description for the sample in the software.
Create a new folder on the PC with the date and a descriptive name; select this as the file location.
Visually confirm the stage is raised for fluidic input.
Press 'GO!' to begin the automated priming procedure. (If priming fails, press 'Stop', then 'Clear constriction', then retry).
Allow the instrument to automatically begin 10-second acquisition measurements (traces).

steps.title: Monitor and Collect Data
steps.instruction: Use the auto-analysis tools to monitor data quality and determine run duration.

substeps.instruction: Use the live CSD tool to select a diameter range and monitor concentration (e.g., continue until 10,000 spike-in beads are measured).
If the live CSD tool is missing, click 'Restart Auto-analysis Engine' under Manual Utilities.
If the instrument clogs (indicated by red Xs), click 'Stop', 'Clear Constriction', and then 'Continuous' to resolve the clog and combine data.

steps.title: End Sample Run
steps.instruction: Stop data collection and remove the cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Press the 'Stop' button once satisfied with the data.
Press the 'End Run' button and allow the sequence to finish until the blue ring light illuminates.
Press the metal button to lower the stage, then remove and discard the used cartridge.

steps.title: Post-Run Data Processing
steps.instruction: Process raw data files into stats files.

substeps.instruction: Open Data Viewer software, select the correct folder, and move all raw files from the run into the 'currently loaded' box.
Click 'Process All' under the Process Raw Data tab to create stat files.
Remove all filters and click 'Combine Data for All Loaded' under the Data Output tab.

steps.title: System Shutdown
steps.instruction: Perform final cleaning and power down the instrument.

substeps.instruction: Load a cleaning cartridge onto the stage and raise the stage.
Select the 'Instrument shut down' button and follow the on-screen instructions.
Leave the DI water bottles attached to the machine to protect lines from contaminants and prevent O-rings from drying out.
